steps.title: Prepare 1× PBS
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.1 g KCl, 0.12 g KH2PO4, 4 g NaCl, and 0.5725 g Na2HPO4 in ~500 mL double‑distilled water, adjust pH to 7.4 with HCl or NaOH, bring volume to 500 mL; store at 24‑26 °C for up to 2 months.

steps.title: Prepare 1× PBST
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL Tween‑20 (0.1 % final) to 50 mL of 1× PBS; store at 4 °C for 2‑3 weeks.

steps.title: Prepare 4 % PFA
steps.instruction: Heat 80 mL 1× PBS to 60 °C in a glass beaker, add 4 g paraformaldehyde, stir until milky, add NaOH beads while mixing, adjust pH to 7.4 with concentrated HCl, bring volume to 100 mL with 1× PBS, aliquot 10 mL into 15 mL sterile tubes, store at –20 °C for 2‑3 weeks; handle in a fume hood with gloves, mask and goggles.

steps.title: Prepare 30 % sucrose
steps.instruction: Dissolve 30 g sucrose in 1× PBS and bring volume to 100 mL; store at 24‑26 °C for up to 2 months.

steps.title: Prepare 0.01 % avidin
steps.instruction: Dissolve 25 mg avidin in 250 mL 1× PBS (0.01 %); aliquot 1 mL portions into 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 0.05 % biotin
steps.instruction: Dissolve 100 mg biotin in 200 mL 1× PBS (0.05 %); aliquot 1 mL portions into 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare Hoechst working solution
steps.instruction: Reconstitute 100 mg Hoechst 33342 in 10 mL 1× PBS to obtain a 10 mg/mL (1000×) stock; add 1 µL stock to 999 µL 1× PBS to make a 10 µg/mL working solution (1 mL total); aliquot 100 µL stock into amber tubes and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Isolate E14.5 fetal livers
steps.instruction: Dissect fetal livers from E14.5 pregnant mouse under ice‑cold conditions.

substeps.instruction: 1. Sacrifice a 14.5‑day pregnant mouse by cervical dislocation (weight gain ≥5 g confirms pregnancy).
2. Wipe abdomen with 70 % ethanol, lift skin with Graefe forceps and make a midline incision with fine scissors; extend cuts laterally to create a C‑shaped opening perpendicular to the midline.
3. Using Graefe forceps, cut the peritoneum to expose the abdominal cavity and visualize uterine horns.
4. Hold the uterus with Graefe forceps, cut distal ends and the centre to excise the uterine horns completely.
5. Transfer uterine horns to a 50 mL sterile polypropylene tube containing ice‑cold 1× PBS to remove excess blood; keep tissues at 4 °C.

6. Place uterine horns in a 100 mm cell‑culture dish with ice‑cold 1× PBS; under a stereo zoom microscope, gently remove endometrial tissue around each conceptus with extra‑fine Graefe and Dumont #5 straight forceps, avoiding placenta puncture.
7. Transfer each conceptus to a fresh 60 mm dish with ice‑cold 1× PBS using Dumont #5/45 bent‑tip forceps.
8. Gently tease away the yolk sac (YS) from the fetus with Dumont #5 straight forceps, taking care not to nick major vessels.
9. Nip the extra‑embryonic vessels (EEVs) that connect the fetus to the placenta.
10. Move the fetus to a new 60 mm dish containing only enough ice‑cold 1× PBS to keep it wet.

11. Using extra‑fine Graefe forceps and Dumont #5 straight forceps, tease away rostral and caudal fetal tissues to expose the fetal liver (FL); avoid direct handling of the FL with forceps and work quickly on ice to limit lysozyme‑mediated degradation.

steps.title: Fix fetal livers in PFA
steps.instruction: Fix isolated FLs with 4 % PFA, then wash.

substeps.instruction: 1. Transfer each FL into a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube containing 1.5 mL ice‑cold 4 % PFA (≈1:20 tissue:fixative ratio).
2. Place tubes horizontally on ice and rocker at 30 rpm for 1 h.
3. Remove PFA, add 1.5 mL 1× PBS for a quick rinse, discard.
4. Add 1.5 mL fresh 1× PBS and incubate 30 min on ice with rocking.
5. Perform two additional 30 min washes with fresh 1× PBS each (total three 30‑min washes). Use careful pipetting (aspirate opposite side of tissue, add buffer against tube wall) to avoid damage.
6. Pause point: FLs in fresh 1× PBS can be stored at 4 °C for up to 2 months before proceeding.

steps.title: Cryo‑protect livers with sucrose
steps.instruction: Incubate FLs in 30 % sucrose for cryoprotection.

substeps.instruction: 1. Remove PBS and add 1.5 mL 30 % sucrose to each tube; place tubes on a tube revolver at 24‑26 °C for 30 s.
2. Transfer tubes to a 4 °C stand and incubate overnight (~16 h) until the FL sinks, indicating complete cryoprotection.

steps.title: Prepare cryo‑mold and snap‑freeze
steps.instruction: Embed cryo‑protected FLs in PolyFreeze and freeze via indirect snap‑freezing.

substeps.instruction: 1. Assemble a disposable plastic mold (15 × 15 × 5 mm) and fill with ~1.5 mL PolyFreeze™ cryo‑matrix.
2. In a stainless‑steel mold (24 × 24 × 10 mm) place ~2 mL 2‑methyl‑butane on crushed dry ice; allow the butane to cool (30–45 s).
3. While the butane cools, gently place the sucrose‑protected FL into the PolyFreeze, fully immersing it.
4. Once the butane is cold, float the plastic mold (containing the FL) on the surface of the 2‑methyl‑butane (do not submerge). The cryo‑matrix will solidify from transparent jelly to a white solid.
5. Transfer the solidified cryo‑block to –80 °C for storage. Pause point: blocks can be stored at –80 °C until downstream immunostaining steps.
